input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes exclusive dealing on Customer — Vendor is the "sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term" — with no category narrowing beyond the whole services line, no 12-month limit, and no performance-based exit. That is the walk-away position (full-term exclusivity with no service-level or delivery-failure termination right), so it fails the fallback. It also directly contradicts Section 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment), so deletion is the smallest edit that both reaches the preferred position and resolves the internal conflict. The fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on missed service levels) is offered in the comment if exclusivity is commercially necessary.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment in Section 2.2, as we do not accept exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations and must remain free to engage other suppliers. It also contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3 (no purchase commitment and no exclusivity); if some exclusivity is commercially important, we could discuss a narrow 12-month category-specific arrangement that ends automatically on any service level or delivery failure.
proposal.summary: Delete Section 2.2 exclusivity obligation binding Customer.
